c.tagline: Elegant City of Churches, with festivals, food, and famous wine at the doorstep.

taxi.fareNote: Fares are metered and a set surcharge applies to airport pickups; book by app or phone, or use ride-hail (Uber, Ola, DiDi).

emergency.note: 000 is Australia's national emergency number for police, fire, and ambulance; 112 also works from any mobile phone.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Hindley Street's late-night bar strip draws rowdy drunken crowds on weekends; keep usual awareness there after midnight.

hood_desc: Adelaide's compact grid heart, ringed by parklands and laced by a free tram line, packed with Rundle Mall shopping, the Central Market, museums, and the North Terrace cultural boulevard; best for first-timers who want everything within an easy walk.

A leafy, heritage district just across the River Torrens, full of bluestone cottages, historic pubs, and the cafe-and-restaurant strips of O'Connell and Melbourne Streets; suits travellers who want a calm, upscale base minutes from the CBD.

Adelaide's classic seaside suburb at the end of the tram line, built around the jetty, Moseley Square, and Glenelg Beach with its Jetty Road dining and sunsets over the Gulf St Vincent; ideal for a relaxed beach-town stay.

A cosmopolitan inner-eastern suburb centred on The Parade, a lively strip of boutiques, cafes, wine bars, and restaurants with a village feel; good for shoppers and diners who want local character away from the tourist core.

A regenerated former industrial pocket just northwest of the CBD, now a walkable, design-led urban village anchored by the Plant 4 food market and street art; suits younger travellers and creatives after a trendy, low-key scene.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink, though some prefer filtered for taste.

transit.hours: Trains and the Glenelg tram run roughly 5am to midnight; the free City Connector buses run about 7am-7:15pm (to 9:15pm on Fridays). Late-night public transport is limited, so ride-hail fills the gap.
transit.pay: Tap on with a metroCARD (a A$5 reloadable smartcard) or the Buy & Go app; peak fares are about A$4.55 (~$3) and off-peak about A$2.60 (~$1.70), with a 2-hour transfer window. The free City Connector buses (routes 98 and 99) and the CBD tram free zone need no ticket at all.

transit.m: JetBus J1/J2 to the city (20-30 min)
Taxi to city centre (12-18 min, includes airport fee)

tip.r: Tipping is not expected in Australia; rounding up the bill or leaving around 10% for excellent service is appreciated but never required.
